text:
The face of the world has changed

since I heard the steps of your soul, light,

oh, very light!, beside me, slipping

between me and the terrible cleft of death

where I thought I would sink, but I was lifted

toward love and came to know a new song

to rock the tides of life.

Thirsty, I drained the cup of bitterness

that God, at birth, gives us;

beside you, my love, I have praised its sweetness.

The names of lands and sky are altered,

they change according to where you are

or may someday be.

Before, I adored this lute and this song of mine

(the angels know it well); I still love them,

only because your name mingles with their rhythm.

translation.title: The Face of the World Has Changed
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps this Spanish variant's fuller music-and-tide phrasing.
